pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Irregularly shaped polygonal dark regions with diffuse edge gradients. Individual patches on the mid-flank exhibit higher spatial area and more defined edges compared to the cranial-dorsal region, where geometry is disrupted by textural anomalies. Edge angularity is moderate, showing sub-rounded to jagged pixel transitions.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: A continuous network of light-toned interstitial pathways separating the patches. The topological graph is composed of 3-way and 4-way junction nodes. Pathway pixel thickness is relatively consistent across the mid-flank but narrows significantly towards the dorsal ridge.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: Low-amplitude, high-frequency serrated silhouette along the upper neck and shoulder. Individual hair-tuft clusters create a jagged 1D geometric contour against the blurred background.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: Extensive clusters of dark, hyper-pigmented, and raised textural nodules are concentrated on the upper neck and transition onto the shoulder. These regions show significant disruption of the standard pelage pattern with crusty, irregular pixel-level detail.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A small avian organism (oxpecker) is perched on the posterior-dorsal region of the rump. Multiple small, dark, circular punctate lesions are visible across the flank, distinct from the primary pelage patches.
other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced skin folds and horizontal wrinkling visible at the ventral-neck and forelimb junction.
